title: "3-7 Exercise 9"
format: html
editor: visual
---

Data from FRED: [Infra-Annual Labor Statistics: Labor Force Total: From 15 to 64 Years for Australia](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/LFAC64TTAUM647S)

## Read the data

```{r}
library(fpp3)
library(readxl)
aus_labor <- read_excel("data/fred-aus-labor-force.xlsx", 
                        sheet = "Monthly", 
                        col_types = c("date", "numeric"),
                        col_names = c('Date', 'Persons'), skip = 1) |> 
    mutate(Month = yearmonth(Date)) |> 
    select(-Date) |>
    as_tsibble(index = Month)
```

## Clean the data

Check to see if there are missing intervals

```{r}

aus_labor |> has_gaps()
```

Looks like we are good. We'll create some here just to show the process.

```{r}
aus_gaps <- aus_labor[c(-3,-6,-9), ]
has_gaps(aus_gaps)
scan_gaps(aus_gaps)
aus_gaps |> fill_gaps() |> filter(Month %in% scan_gaps(aus_gaps)$Month)
aus_gaps |> fill_gaps() |> pull(Month) |> identical(aus_labor$Month)
```

```{r}
aus_labor |> 
    autoplot(Persons) +
    ggtitle('Australian Labor Force') +
    scale_y_continuous("People '000s", labels = scales::label_comma(scale = 1/1000))
```

Reproduce Figure 3.19 from [3.7 Exercises](https://otexts.com/fpp3/decomposition-exercises.html)

Note: The date range of this dataset differs slightly from Figure 3.19. We'll ignore that here.

```{r}
aus_labor |> 
    model(STL = STL(Persons)) |> 
    components() |> 
    autoplot()
```

```{r}
aus_labor |> 
    model(STL = STL(Persons ~ season(window = 'periodic') + trend(window = 12))) |> 
    components() |> 
    autoplot()
```

Experiments:

-   Try adding period = `n * 12` for different values of `n`
-   What happens to the `Remainder` when the trend window is increased?
-   What happens to the `Remainder` when the trend window is decreased to 1?

```{r}
aus_labor |> 
    model(classical_decomposition(Persons)) |> 
    components() |> 
    autoplot()
```
